title: Busy lives
goals: Talk about what you did, using regular verbs in the simple past (watched, studied, chatted).
Use very common irregular verbs in the past (went, had, bought, took, wrote).
Say what you didn't do with didn't, and ask questions with Did and What did…?
Place events in time with yesterday, last night, two days ago.
Order a story with before, after, when, and then, using commas correctly.
React to news with Congratulations!, Good luck!, I'm sorry to hear that, and You did?

learn.title: Simple past: regular verbs
learn.html:
The simple past describes actions that finished at a moment in the past (yesterday, last Saturday, two days ago). It is the same for all persons: I watched, she watched, they watched. With regular verbs, add -ed.

RuleVerb → past
Regular: + -edwatch → watched, cook → cooked, play → played
Ends in -e: + -dinvite → invited, like → liked
Consonant + y: y → i + -edstudy → studied, try → tried
Vowel + y: + -edplay → played, stay → stayed
One-syllable CVC: double the final consonantchat → chatted, stop → stopped

Pronunciation of -ed: /t/ (watched, cooked), /d/ (played, studied), and /ɪd/ after t or d (invited, wanted). Time signals for the past: yesterday, last night, two days ago, on Monday.

watch.why: Consonant + y: y changes to i + -ed.
In the past, the regular verb takes -ed.
The past doesn't change with he/she: no -s.

learn.title: Simple past: irregular verbs
learn.html:
Many very common verbs don't follow the -ed rule: they have their own past form. You have to learn them by heart. They are also the same for all persons.

BasePastBasePast
gowentmakemade
havehadmeetmet
dodidreadread (spelled the same, sounds like /red/)
buyboughtseesaw
getgottaketook
eatatewritewrote

Examples: I went to the bank. She bought new shoes. We had a piano lesson. Don't add -ed to these verbs.

learn.title: Negatives and questions in the past: didn't and Did
learn.html:
For negatives and questions we use the auxiliary did, and the main verb goes back to its base form (no -ed and no irregular form). The auxiliary already shows the past.

TypeStructureExample
Negativesubject + didn't + base verbI didn't work late. She didn't go out.
Yes/no questionDid + subject + base verb?Did you meet your friends?
Short answerYes, subject + did. / No, subject + didn't.Yes, I did. / No, we didn't.
Wh- questionWh- + did + subject + base verb?What did you do last weekend?

Didn't = did not. This applies to regular and irregular verbs: I didn't watch, I didn't buy.

watch.why: After didn't, use the base verb.

watch.wrong: Did you went to the party?
watch.right: Did you go to the party?
watch.why: After did, use the base verb.
The short answer ends in did.

learn.title: Ordering events: before, after, when, and then
learn.html:
To describe a sequence of actions, we use order words. Before, after, and when can go at the start or in the middle. Then starts the next sentence.

WordUseExample
beforeearlier than somethingI made a list before I went shopping.
afterlater than somethingAfter I finished work, I went to the gym.
whenat the time something happenedWhen I got home, I took a shower.
thennext, after thatI ate dinner. Then I washed the dishes.

Punctuation: if before, after, or when starts the sentence, put a comma after that part: After class, I went home. If they are in the middle, there is no comma: I went home after class.

watch.wrong: After I finished work I went home.
watch.right: After I finished work, I went home.
watch.why: Opening clause: comma before the next part.
No comma if after is in the middle.

watch.wrong: I ate dinner. After, I washed the dishes.
watch.right: I ate dinner. Then I washed the dishes.
watch.why: For the next action, use then; after needs something after it (after dinner).

learn.title: Reacting to news
learn.html:
• Congratulations! / Good for you! — good news: I passed my test! — Congratulations!
  • Good luck! — something that is going to happen: I have an interview tomorrow. — Good luck!
  • That's great news! — very good news.
  • I'm sorry to hear that. / Oh no! — bad news: I had a cold all week. — I'm sorry to hear that.
  • You did? / Did you? — to show interest or surprise. The auxiliary is repeated: I got a new job. — You did?
  • What happened? — asking for more details.

write.prompt: Write a paragraph of 60 to 100 words about what you did last weekend. Use regular and irregular verbs, a negative with didn't, and the words before, after, when, or then. Starter: Last weekend, I …

At least three irregular verbs (went, had, bought…)
A negative with didn't + base verb
An order word (after, then…), with a comma if it starts the sentence
Between 60 and 100 words
write.model: Last weekend, I stayed at home on Saturday morning. I cleaned my room and washed my clothes. Then I went to the market and bought some fruit. After that, I had lunch with my mother. In the afternoon, I watched a movie. I didn't go out at night because I was tired. On Sunday, I visited my grandmother. When I got home, I cooked dinner and called my friend. It was a nice weekend.

write.prompt: Write a 6-line dialogue with a friend. He tells you some news (good or bad), you react with a suitable expression, and you ask him two questions with Did or What did. Starter: A: I got a new job! B: You did? Congratulations! …
checklist: 6 lines, two people
An appropriate reaction (Congratulations!, I'm sorry to hear that…)
You did? or Did you? to show interest
Two questions with Did / What did + base verb
Short answers (Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.)
write.model:
A: I got a new job!
B: You did? Congratulations! What did you do before this job?
A: I worked in a small shop for two years, and last month I decided to look for something new.
B: Did you like your first day? Did you eat lunch with the team?
A: Yes, I did. It was great. And no, I didn't eat with them. I was too busy!
B: That's okay. I'm happy for you. Let's celebrate this weekend!

reading.title: A very busy week
reading.intro: Read María's email to her friend and answer.
paragraphs: Hi Laura! Sorry I didn't write last week. I had a really busy week. On Monday, I worked late because I wrote a long report for my boss. I didn't cook dinner, so I bought tacos on the way home. After dinner, I made a list of things to do.

On Tuesday, I ran errands. First, I went to the bank. Then I bought some food at the supermarket and met my sister for coffee. We talked for an hour. When I got home, I practiced the piano for thirty minutes. I'm not very good, but I love it!

On Wednesday, I took an English exam. I studied for three nights before the exam, and I passed! My teacher said, "Congratulations!" I felt so happy. On Thursday, I had an interview at a new company. I didn't sleep well the night before, but the interview went well. They called me on Friday, and I got the job! I called my mom, and she felt so proud.

On Saturday, I invited some friends over. We ate pizza, watched a movie, and chatted until midnight. On Sunday, I stayed home and rested. I didn't do anything at all! After that week, I felt exhausted. What did you do last weekend? Write soon! Love, María

happy and pleased about something you did
to rest and stop working or moving

listening.title: What did you do last weekend?
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Hi, Sofia! What did you do last weekend?
Hi, Dan! I had a great weekend. On Saturday, I went to my cousin's birthday party.
You did? Did you take a gift?
Yes, I did. I bought her a new bag. After the party, I went home and watched a movie.
I didn't watch a new movie. I saw an old comedy again. Then I went to bed early.
On Sunday, I stayed home. I cooked a big lunch for my parents. When we finished, I washed the dishes.
And you? Did you go out?
No, I didn't. I worked all weekend. I wrote a report for my boss.
Oh, I'm sorry to hear that.
It's OK. I finished it last night, so today I'm free!
